title: Coin Path
summary: Given an integer array coins of length n and an integer maxJump, find the path from index 1 to index n with the minimum cost.
statement: Given an integer array coins of length n and an integer maxJump, find the path from index 1 to index n with the minimum cost. You can jump to any index i if coins[i] is not -1 and you must pay coins[i]. You can only jump to indices i + k where i + k <= n and k is in the range [1, maxJump]. Return the indices of the path in order, ensuring the cost is minimized and the path is lexicographically smallest if there are multiple paths with the same cost. If reaching index n is impossible, return an empty array.
constraints: 1 <= len(coins) <= 1,000; -1 marks a blocked position; max_jump is positive.
Return one-based indices minimizing paid coin cost; break cost ties lexicographically, or return [] if unreachable.
hints: The best suffix from each index determines the best full route.
Work backward and compare candidates by (total cost, full path).
For each reachable index, prepend it to every reachable next state and retain the smallest pair.
Tuple ordering enforces cost first and lexicographic path second without a separate tie-reconstruction pass.
editorial: Tuple ordering enforces cost first and lexicographic path second without a separate tie-reconstruction pass.

tests.explanation: The path 1,3,5 is the minimum-cost reachable route.
Paths 1,2,4 and 1,3,4 tie in cost, so 1,2,4 is lexicographically smaller.
